subject: NovusPay pilot: cost framing, levers to hit procurement target
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@novuspay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: NovusPay pilot: cost framing, levers to hit procurement target

Hi Samir — thanks again for the time today. Quick post-call recap and a concrete set of options so procurement has something to evaluate. I pulled together an initial estimate (attached) and highlighted the practical levers we discussed that will materially affect token spend.

TL;DR
- Primary pain: token-driven spend on customer-facing chat flows at peak + lack of predictable unit economics for new features.
- Goal: run a 3-week pilot to validate quality & cost controls, then move to a staged rollout if pilot meets ROI thresholds.
- Two compressed options below (minimal vs recommended) with expected token spend and major assumptions. Detailed estimate attached.

Recap of needs we heard
- Tight quarterly budget (~$25–35k) for initial validation period.
- Peak-latency targets (<250ms tail) for checkout-related flows; they will tolerate slight increases during heavy load for the pilot if cost savings are realized.
- Security gating: SOC2 + IP assurances required before production.

Levers we can use (impact estimates)
- Batching + request shaping: reduce per-token GPU allocation and amortize overhead (estimated 25–40% token cost reduction on high-throughput endpoints).
- Prefix/KV caching for repeated context (chat/email templates): 15–25% token reduction for conversational flows with reuse.
- Model selection & quantization: swap to a lighter verified variant for non-critical flows (10–30% cost delta depending on quality acceptance).
- Routing by policy: route non-critical traffic to cheaper capacity during peak.

Pilot options (summary)
- Option A — Discovery/Proof: 2 endpoints, shared hosted capacity, focus on batching + caching. Estimated token spend: $11,500 over 3 weeks. (Minimal security package)
- Option B — Validation (recommended): 4 endpoints, reserved modest capacity window to control latency, full batching + prefix caching + quality guardrails. Estimated token spend: $27,800 over 3 weeks. (Includes SOC2 evidence package + engineer support)

Assumptions in estimate (see attached tab)
- Usage profile: 35k requests/day across endpoints with 120 tokens/request average for chat flows (we used your sample traces).
- Effective batching window: 30–50ms, achievable with current traffic shapes per your engineering notes.
- Caching hit-rate: 20% conservative baseline for first pilot.

Next steps I propose
1) Confirm which option (A or B) aligns with procurement target — I can compress Option B to reduce spend if needed.
2) If Option B: we’ll send a short MSA + pilot SOW and a DocuSign link; engineering kickoff within 3 business days after PO.
3) Security packet: we’ll provide SOC2 summary + standard controls; if you need the full artifact we can schedule an audit-sharing session.

Attachments: novuspay-pilot-estimate-20280715.xlsx, redwood-pilot-mpa-draft-20280715.pdf

Thanks — I’ll be on standby to re-scope the numbers to hit a tighter procurement ceiling.

—
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[t] +1 415-555-0123 | tessa.morgan@redwood.com

From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@novuspay.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@novuspay.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Jul 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NovusPay pilot: cost framing, levers to hit procurement target

Thanks for the clear recap, Tessa — helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side: 

- Confirming budget guidance: we have capacity at the top end of that range (~$30k) but procurement will push to the low end if we can get a narrower scope.
- Prioritization: we want to validate customer-facing chat flows first (two high-volume endpoints). If the recommended Option B is the better technical validation, can we compress scope (fewer endpoints) to match the $30k target?
- Security: SOC2 summary + a short NDA should be enough to start; procurement will need the MSA and the pilot SOW to issue a PO (timeline attached).

I attached our internal procurement timeline and notes — procurement lead is Priya (cc’d). If you can provide a reduced-cost Option B (same controls, smaller capacity window) that lands ~30k we can move quickly.

On the latency piece: we care most about p95 during checkout flows — if you can show the latency profile for reserved modest capacity in your estimate, that will help sign-off.

Samir
CTO, NovusPay
samir.khan@novuspay.com

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@novuspay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Jul 2028 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: NovusPay pilot: cost framing, levers to hit procurement target

Samir — appreciate the quick reply and the procurement timeline. I reworked the numbers and compressed a recommended-path option to land near $30k while preserving the validation signal you need. See the options below and I’ve updated the attached spreadsheet with the trimmed capacity window and expected latency profile for reserved modest capacity.

Updated options
- Option A (unchanged) — Discovery: $11,500 — 2 endpoints, hosted shared capacity. Minimal evidence.

- Option B-Compact (new) — Validation compressed to fit $30k target: $29,400
  - 3 endpoints (two high-volume chat endpoints + one low-volume support routing endpoint)
  - Reserved modest capacity during business hours (08:00–20:00 local) to keep p95 < 300ms for checkout flows; background traffic routed to cheaper capacity.
  - Batching + prefix/KV caching enabled at pilot start; target caching hit of 20–30% depending on traffic.
  - Includes SOC2 summary, pilot SOW, 4 hours engineering onboarding, and one weekly sync.

Key assumptions for B-Compact
- Average tokens/request: 120; peak concurrency windows aligned with your provided traces.
- Effective batching reduces compute per token by ~33% on high-throughput endpoints; effective caching hit 22% in week 1 (assume rising with tuning).
- Savings vs baseline: modeled as a reduction of 30–38% in effective token cost when combined levers apply.

ROI framing (3-week pilot)
- If pilot traffic shapes hold and we hit the modeled hit rates, we expect a 6–9x marginal return in terms of avoided run-rate when extrapolated to a 90-day rollout for the same traffic (largely from batching + routing savings).
- For a $29.4k pilot, projected monthly run-rate savings post-rollout could be $18–30k depending on rollout aggressiveness.

Deliverables we’ll send in parallel
- Pilot SOW + MSA (DocuSign link)
- SOC2 summary + security controls mapping
- Updated estimate workbook with per-endpoint token curves and latency profiles

Ask from your side
1) Confirm B-Compact aligns with procurement target and we’ll send DocuSign SOW.
2) Share a preferred start date window (we can schedule engineering kickoff within 3 business days of signed SOW + PO).

I can also do a short call with Priya + procurement if that helps move the PO faster — happy to join.

Attachments: novuspay-pilot-estimate-20280715.xlsx, redwood-pilot-mpa-draft-20280715.pdf

—
Tessa Morgan
